proposal.title: Anchor-Decoupled Mask-Invariant Boosting (ADMIB) for tabular classification under missingness shift
proposal.hypothesis: When features are missing, a native-NaN booster learns two signals: what the missing values were, and how often features go missing in training. Removing the second signal should improve mean average precision (mAP) on held-out MNAR and structural masks at a small clean-data cost. The method only works when the label-relevant signal can be recovered from always-observed anchors plus observed values.
proposal.mechanism: Native-NaN splits (1603.02754v3) send missing rows to a learned default direction. That direction encodes P(Y|M) learned under training MCAR. When the mechanism shifts, the target P(Y|X_obs,M) changes (2603.17599v1, 2406.16484v1). ADMIB has three parts. First, it builds a pattern-neutral imputation from the anchors only. Second, it adds an iterative completion step. Third, it trains under resampled masks of several types, so that mask-indicator splits no longer predict the label. This targets the mask-to-label causal path directly, rather than adding preprocessing.

proposed_primitives.definition: For each non-anchor feature j, fit E[x_j | anchors x0,x1, other observed values] on rows where j is observed in training. Fill missing entries with predictions. Never use labels or clean values.

Add extra masks per batch from a family: MCAR at rates 0.2–0.5, MAR driven by anchor quantiles, and block masks over random feature groups. Mask probabilities are computed from observed or imputed values only.

Reweight training rows by inverse P(M-pattern cluster | anchors, imputed X). This makes the mask approximately independent of Y given the completed features. Weights enter only the tree loss, with no scaler afterwards, so they cannot cancel algebraically.

relations.counterfactual_prediction: Removing it brings back NaN default-direction reliance, and held-out MNAR mAP drops.
Without it, the weights collapse to near-uniform under MCAR, and there is no gain over the imputer alone.
Removing it raises validation-MAR mAP but lowers reversed-MNAR mAP.

assumptions: Held-out MNAR is restricted to self-masking where the missing values are partly predictable from the anchors and observed features. Under this assumption the Bayes predictor of the mask-agnostic target is shared across mechanisms.

Failure case: if a missing value carries label information that cannot be predicted from observed variables, no mask-agnostic method can recover it. The method then underperforms the native-NaN model on same-direction MNAR, where the mask itself is informative.
No unlabeled target-batch statistics are used.
The 5 redundant features are linear combinations, so imputation from anchors and observed features is feasible.
strongest_prior_art: 2507.08280v2 (MIRRAMS): overlaps in aiming for mask-robust, label-relevant features. It differs by using deep mutual-information losses. ADMIB uses tree weighting and imputation.
2106.00311v2: overlaps on impute-then-regress. It differs by not addressing mechanism shift.
2406.16484v1: diagnosis of ignorable versus non-ignorable shifts only, with no proposed method.
algorithm: Split the data 60/20/20. Training data keeps its native MCAR20% masks.
Fit the anchor-conditional imputer on observed training entries only.
Sample K=3 extra masks per row from the mechanism family and apply them on top of the existing missingness.
Fit a pattern classifier P(cluster | anchors, imputed X) and compute clipped inverse weights.
Train HistGradientBoosting on imputed X with the weights. No mask indicators are given as inputs.
Select hyperparameters by mean mAP across the clean, MCAR20, MCAR40 and MAR validation masks.
Evaluate once on the three held-out mechanisms.
proposal.baseline: Native-NaN HistGradientBoosting. Second baseline: the same model plus random MCAR mask augmentation. Strongest constituent baseline: NeuMiss-style joint impute-and-regress (2106.00311v2), implemented as an MLP small enough for CPU.
ablations: Remove the imputer and use native NaN, keeping resampling and weights.
Add mask indicators as features, to test whether the mask-to-label path returns.
Replace the anchor-conditional imputer with mean imputation.
Match the total number of augmented rows across all arms.
proposal.metric: Primary: mean mAP across the three held-out mechanisms. Secondary: Brier score, clean-data mAP, and the worst-mechanism mAP. All reported as 10-seed means with paired bootstrap confidence intervals.
proposal.falsification: Reject the hypothesis if either condition holds: (a) ADMIB's held-out mean mAP fails to beat native NaN plus augmentation by at least 0.01, with the paired 95% confidence interval excluding 0; or (b) ablations show that the weights or the imputer contribute no measurable gain. Also report whether clean-data mAP drops by more than 0.02.
proposal.feasibility: Each seed involves 3000 training rows ×4 copies, about 20 imputation regressions, and one booster, which should take under 90 seconds on a laptop CPU.

validation_note: Revalidated saved response: proposed primitive names need not have a specific prefix; known arXiv aliases normalized; grounded edge endpoints included in component list. No semantic content or model calls added.
